title: Talking about past experiences / Kuganira ku byatumye ubushake
bridge: Mu gaciri, kugana ku byatumye ubushake tubikora ubwoko bw'imperatif parfait ('he visitado') cyangwa pretérito indefinido ('visité'), kugeza ahantu haba hamwe n'ubushake cyangwa oya. Mu Icyongereza, kugana ku byatumye ubushake tubikora 'present perfect' ('have visited'), utubabaje ntabwo hari ikibanjijwe mu gaciri. Ikintu gisobanutse ni uko mu Icyongereza tubikora 'have + participio' kugana ku gikorwa mu gihe atari ubwise, kandi mu gaciri tubikora pretérito indefinido kugana ku gikorwa mu gihe kisezerwa. Menya: mu Icyongereza nta 'present perfect' ubikorwa na amagambo yo kuganira ku gihe cyashize kose nk' 'yesterday' cyangwa 'last year'.
rule: Kugana ku byatumye ubushake mu Icyongereza, tubikora 'present perfect' na ubwoko bw' have/has + participio cyashize. Bikorwa kugana ku: 1) byatumye ubushake atari ubwise igihe (I have visited Paris), 2) gikorwa cyashize kandi bifite ubushake mu mbara (She has lost her keys), 3) na amagambo nk' 'ever', 'never', 'already', 'yet', 'just', 'before'. Ubwoko bw'ahantu bukorwa na 'have not' (haven't) cyangwa 'has not' (hasn't). Ubwoko bw'ibibazo birinda ubusubirizi bw'ubufasha (Have you ever...?). Kugana ku byatumye ubushake, tubikora 'Have you ever + participio?' kandi dusubiza na 'Yes, I have' cyangwa 'No, I never have'. Nta 'present perfect' ubikorwa na amagambo yo kuganira ku gihe cyashize kose (yesterday, last week, in 2010). Mu bihe bitari ubwise, tubikora 'past simple' (visited, went). Kugira ngo A2, bikorwa neza kumenya participios y'amagambo yose (go-gone, eat-eaten, see-seen, have-had).

concept_examples.text: I have visited Mexico.
She has never eaten sushi.
Have you ever seen that movie?
We have already finished our homework.

common_error.explanation: Iyi ngororero igomba kubera mu gaciri ubwo hari 'Nyamuneka naje mu Paris yesterday' mu bindi mibare, ariko mu Icyongereza 'present perfect' atikoranijwe na amagambo yo kuganira ku gihe cyashize kose nk' 'yesterday'. Kugana ku gihe kisezerwa mu bashize, bikorwa 'past simple' (visited). Ntidushobora kumenya igihe, tubikora 'present perfect' (have visited). Menya: 'present perfect' + gihe kisezerwa = si yo.

examples.original: Have you ever been to London?
examples.note: Tubikora 'ever' mu ibibazo kugana ku byatumye ubushake mu gihe kose mu ubushake.

examples.original: I have never tried Thai food.
examples.note: 'Never' bikorwa hagati y' 'have' na participio, kandi bishimira 'nta nshuro' mu ubushake.

examples.original: She has never flown in a plane.
examples.phonetic: /ʃi hæz ˈnɛvər floʊn ɪn ə pleɪn/
examples.note: Menya ko 'flown' ni participio y' 'fly', igambi ry'irangi.
'Already' bikorwa mu magambo kandi bishimira 'nyamuneka' (bigeze mu gihe kisezerwa).

examples.original: Have you bought the tickets yet?
examples.note: 'Yet' bikorwa mu ibibazo kandi mu magambo, mu mwisho y'igambi, kandi bishimira 'bigeze/bigeze'.

examples.original: We haven't finished our project yet.
examples.note: Mu magambo, 'yet' bikorwa mu mwisho kandi bishimira ko ikintu kirabigeze kigashye.

examples.translation: Nyamuneka naje mu Peru (mu gihe kose mu ubushake).
examples.note: 'Present perfect' bikorwa atari ubwise igihe, kugana ku byatumye ubushake.

examples.phonetic: /aɪ wɛnt tə pəˈruː ɪn tuː ˈθaʊzənd nɪnˈtiːn/
examples.note: 'Past simple' bikorwa na amagambo yo kuganira ku gihe cyashize kose, nk' 'in 2019'.

examples.original: She has lived in Madrid for two years.
examples.phonetic: /ʃi hæz lɪvd ɪn məˈdrɪd fɔːr tuː jɪrz/
examples.translation: Yaremye yabanye mu Madrid mu myaka ibiri.
examples.note: 'Present perfect' bikorwa na 'for' + igihe kugana ku gikorwa kigashye mu mbara.
Mu 'past simple', igambi 'see' bigaragara 'saw', kandi bikorwa na gihe kisezerwa.

title: Making Plans and Arrangements / Gutegura n'ibintu
bridge: Mu gaciri, tubika ubwoko bw'imperatifi bwo mu bushake cyangwa ubwoko bw'imishyikirano (kugenda + infinitif) kugira ngo dufate ibintu. Mu Icyongereza, kuri ibintu n'amategeko, tubika 'present continuous' (I'm meeting) kuri ibintu bifite ubwoko, na 'be going to' (I'm going to visit) kuri ibyishimo. Kanga ubwoba: mu Icyongereza, ntibika ubwoko bw'imperatifi bwo mu bushake kuri ibyishimo by'umuntu, nyamara mu gaciri, hoba (eg. 'Te llamo mañana' → 'I'll call you tomorrow', si 'I call you'). Nanone, 'will' bika kuri ibyishimo by'umuntu, si kuri ibintu bifite ubwoko.
rule:
Kugira ngo ubike ibintu n'amategeko mu Icyongereza ku murongo wa A2, bika ibyo bikorwa:

1. **Present continuous** (am/is/are + -ing): kuri ibintu n'amategeko bifite ubwoko, na igihe n'ahantu. Eg. 'I'm seeing the doctor at 3.' (Nafashe amategeko).

2. **Be going to** (am/is/are going to + infinitif): kuri ibyishimo cyangwa ibintu by'umuntu bitagira ibyerekeretswa. Eg. 'We're going to visit our grandparents.' (Tufite ibyishimo).

3. **Will** (will + verbe base): kuri ibyishimo byafashwe mu gihe waduha, ibyishimo cyangwa ibyishimo. Eg. 'I'll help you with that.' (Ibyishimo by'umuntu).

4. **Would like to** (would like to + infinitif): kuri ibyishimo cyangwa ibintu by'umuntu bya kuri buri wese. Eg. 'Would you like to come to my party?'

Kanga ubwoba ko mu Icyongereza, ntibika ubwoko bw'imperatifi bwo mu bushake kuri ibyishimo by'umuntu (mu kinyejana na gaciri mu bimwe bindi). Bika 'be going to' cyangwa 'present continuous' kuri ibintu.

title: Giving advice and recommendations / Gutanga ibiranga n’ibiranga
bridge: Mu gaciri, kugutanga ibiranga bikoresheje umubare w’ibiryumvenso (te recomiendo que vayas, deberías ir). Mu Icyongereza, umubare w’ibiryumvenso ntibikoreshwa nyuma y’‘recommend’ cyangwa ‘suggest’; tukoresha umubare w’ishusho w’ishura cyangwa inyubako + infinitif: ‘I recommend you go’, ‘I suggest you try’. Tukoreshije ‘should’ (deberías) kuba ari cyiza kurusha ‘must’. Ibibazo bikomeye ni gufata umubare w’ibiryumvenso w’Ikinyarwanda: ‘I recommend that you go’ ni cyo k’ukuri, ariko ‘I recommend you to go’ ni ibibazo bikomeye kuba mu Icyongereza ‘recommend’ ntibikurikirana na ‘to’ kuri infinitif.
rule:
Kugutanga ibiranga n’ibiranga mu Icyongereza ku murongo A2, koresha ibyo bikurikira bya mbere:
1. **Should / Shouldn't + umubare w’ishusho w’ishura**: kugutanga ibiranga by’ingenerwaho. Ese: 'You should eat more vegetables.' 'You shouldn't stay up late.' (ishusho ry’ibyangombwa). Ntikigombwa (he should, no he shoulds).
2. **You could + umubare w’ishusho w’ishura**: kugutanga ibiranga byiza cyangwa ibikubiyemo. Ese: 'You could try yoga.'
3. **I recommend / I suggest + that + inyubako + umubare w’ishusho w’ishura** (nti ‘to’ kandi nti umubare w’ibiryumvenso w’ishusho ry’ishusho). Ese: 'I recommend that you see a doctor.' Ubwo ushaka, koresha umubare w’ishusho w’ishura: 'I recommend seeing a doctor.' cyangwa 'I suggest trying this.'
4. **How about + umubare w’ishusho w’ishura (-ing)?**: kugutanga ibiranga by’ikinyoma. Ese: 'How about going for a walk?'
5. **Why don't you + umubare w’ishusho w’ishura?**: kugutanga ibiranga mu buryo bwa ibibazo. Ese: 'Why don't you take a break?'
Ishusho: nti ‘must’ kugutanga ibiranga, ari cyiteze; ‘must’ ni ububasha. Kugutanga ibiranga byiza, koresha ‘could’ cyangwa ‘might’. Remera ko nyuma y’‘recommend’ na ‘suggest’, nti ‘to’ nyuma y’inyubako: 'I recommend you to go' ntiby’ukuri.

concept_examples.text: You should drink more water.
I recommend that you talk to the teacher.
concept_examples.phonetic: /aɪ ˌrekəˈmend ðæt juː tɔːk tə ðə ˈtiːtʃər/

concept_examples.text: Why don't you try it?
How about studying with us?

common_error.wrong: I recommend you to go to the doctor.
common_error.correct: I recommend that you go to the doctor.
common_error.correct_alt: I recommend going to the doctor.
common_error.explanation: Mu gaciri, tugamba ‘te recomiendo que vayas’ cyangwa ‘te recomiendo ir’, ariko mu Icyongereza, nyuma y’‘recommend’ nti umubare w’infinitif na ‘to’ nyuma y’inyubako. Ishusho ry’ukuri ni ‘recommend + that + inyubako + umubare w’ishusho w’ishura’ cyangwa ‘recommend + umubare w’ishusho w’ishura’. Ibibazo bikiye kuba abanyeshuri bashinjira ‘te recomiendo a ti ir’ (bifashishijwe nka ‘recommend you to go’). Kugira ngo ubihe ibibazo, remera: ‘recommend’ bikurikirana na ‘that’ cyangwa na ‘-ing’, ariko nti na ‘to’.

examples.note: Koresha ‘should’ + umubare w’ishusho w’ishura. Mu gaciri, ‘deberías’ + infinitif.

examples.original: He shouldn't eat so much sugar.
examples.note: Ishusho ry’ibyangombwa ni ‘shouldn't’ + umubare w’ishusho w’ishura. Ntikigombwa kuri yabaye.

examples.original: We should study for the test.
examples.note: ‘Should’ ntibishinjirana na umuntu: I should, you should, we should.

title: Expressing opinions / Kugena ibitekerezo (Ntekereza, Nzemera)
bridge: Mu gihugu cy'Espanya, ‘creo que’ na ‘pienso que’ bikoreshwa bimeze nk’ikintu kimwe, ariko mu linyarwanda hari ibyerekana: ‘Ntekereza’ birimo ibyerekana kurushaho kandi bikoreshwa mu by’ibitekerezo n’iby’ikimenyetso, ‘Nzemera’ birimo ibyerekana gukomeye canke kuri wawe. Ikibazo kinini ni guhindura ‘Yo pienso que’ kuba ‘Ntekereza ko’, ariko mu linyarwanda ‘ko’ ni ikintu gishobora kuba canke atari, kandi kinini cyane kuba atari. Nanone, mu linyarwanda, umubare wa majambo n’uburyo bwo kugena ni uwo mubiri: umuntu + igikorwa + ikiganiro. Reba neza uburyo bwo kugena n’uburyo bwo kushyiraho ‘ko’ ntibishobora kuba byinshi.
rule:
Kugena ibitekerezo mu linyarwanda mu mubare w’A2, tukoresha uburyo bw’urushoho bw’urupfu:
- ‘Ntekereza (ko) + igikorwa’ – kugena ibitekerezo n’iby’ikimenyetso by’umunyama.
- ‘Nzemera (ko) + igikorwa’ – kugena iby’ubushobozi canke iby’ubwenge bwawe.
- ‘Mu buryo bw’ibitekerezo byanjye, + igikorwa’ – birimo ibyerekana gukomeye, ariko kinini mu guandika.
Ibindi bindi bitangwa: ‘Ntekereza ko’ (ntekereza) na ‘Ntekereza ko’ (ntekereza), ubiriwe buri mubiri.
Reba: ‘ko’ ni ikintu gishobora kuba canke atari, kandi kinini cyane kuba atari mu kuganira. Umubare wa majambo n’uburyo bwo kugena ni uwo mubiri: umuntu + igikorwa + ikiganiro. Ntukoreshe ‘of’ canke ‘on’ nyuma ya ‘tekereza/zemera’. Ntuvuga ‘Ntekereza mu ko’, ahubwo vuga ‘Ntekereza ko’ canke ‘Ntekereza’. Inyu: ‘Ntekereza (ko) ni ibyiza’, ‘Nzemera (ko) yari yemeze’. Mu ibibazo by’umunyama, ushobora kushyiraho ‘witekereza?’ nyuma: ‘Ni ibyiza, witekereza?’

In my opinion, this movie is great.

examples.note: Koresha ‘iyi’ kuri ikintu kigaragara; ‘iry’ kuri ikintu kiragara kure.

title: Agreeing and Disagreeing / Gutangaza ubutegetsi n’ubwenge
bridge: Mu gaciri, kugira ubutegetsi tubwira tuti ‘ndabutegetsi’, n’ubwenge tubwira tuti ‘si ndabutegetsi’, ariko mu Icyongereza bashimira amagambo menshi n’ibanga nk’ ‘I agree’ na ‘I disagree’. No kandi ni byaba bikaze kubwira ‘so do I’ na ‘neither do I’ kugira ubutegetsi mu kwemeza cyangwa guhakanisha, ibintu bitagira icyo kibaza mu gaciri kandi bitagira icyo kibaza. Wibuke ko ‘agree’ ni umusoboti, si igisubizo, bityo ntubwire ‘I am agree’, ahubwo ubwire ‘I agree’.
rule: Kugira ubutegetsi mu Icyongereza tubwira tuti ‘I agree’ (ndabutegetsi) cyangwa ‘I think so’ (ntekereza ko ari byo). Kugira ubwenge, tubwira tuti ‘I disagree’ (si ndabutegetsi) cyangwa ‘I don’t think so’ (si ntekereza ko ari byo). Kugira ubutegetsi mu kwemeza ibyo wemeze, tubwira tuti ‘So do I’ (nanjye no) cyangwa ‘Me too’ (nanjye no). Kugira ubutegetsi mu guhakanisha, tubwira tuti ‘Neither do I’ (nanjye nti) cyangwa ‘Me neither’ (nanjye nti). No kandi dutashobora kugira ‘Exactly’ (ni byo) cyangwa ‘That’s right’ (ni byo) kugira ngo dufise ubutegetsi, na ‘I’m not sure’ (si wisigaye) kugira ubwenge bw’umwanya. Wibuke ko ‘agree’ ni umusoboti w’umwanya: I agree, you agree, he/she agrees. Kugira ubwishingiza umwishingiza, tubwira tuti ‘Do you agree?’ (wibutegetsi?)

concept_examples.text: I agree with you.
I disagree with that idea.
So do I.
Neither do I.

common_error.explanation: Ibi bikorwa kubera mu gaciri ‘gutegetsi’ bishimira umusoboti ‘estar’ + igisubizo, n’abanyamakuru bashitondetse mu buryo bw’ibanga bati ‘I am agree’. Mu Icyongereza, ‘agree’ ni umusoboti, bityo atashaka umusoboti ‘to be’. Kugira ngo ubihindure, wibuke ko ‘agree’ ni igikorwa, si umwanya. Kozura n’amagambo nk’ ‘I agree’ cyangwa ‘I don’t agree’.

levels.label: Basic Agreement and Disagreement
levels.translation: Gutangaza ubutegetsi n’ubwenge mu buryo bw’umwanya

examples.note: Uburyo bw’umwanya bwo kugira ubutegetsi. Bishimira mu mibandazwa n’ibindi bintu.
Uburyo bw’ibanga bwo kugira ubwenge. Ubushimire neza kugira ngo ubushimire.
Uburyo bwo kwemeza ko ibintu byari neza.
Uburyo bw’umwanya bwo kugira ubwenge.

levels.label: Agreeing with Positive and Negative Statements

examples.note: Bishimira kugira ubutegetsi mu kwemeza ibyo wemeze. Ahubwo: I like coffee. So do I.
Ikindi kiganiro gikomeye n’ikimwanya kuri byo wemeze.
Bishimira kugira ubutegetsi mu guhakanisha. Ahubwo: I don’t like tea. Neither do I.
Uburyo bw’umwanya bwo ‘Neither do I’.
Uburyo bw’umwanya bwo kugira ubwenge bw’ibanga.
Bishimira kugira ubwenge bw’umwanya.
Wemeza ibintu wibwira mbere yo kugira ubwenge.
Uburyo bw’umwanya bwo kugira ubwenge.

title: Describing Daily Routines / Kugena iby’uburo
bridge: Mu gaciri, uvuga uti ‘nmeza’ cyangwa ‘meza’ ubishusha amagambo yo kwirinda. Mu Icyongereza, ntibishushwa amagambo yo kwirinda mu kugena uburo: ubishusha ‘I get up’. Nanone, mu gaciri akenshi ubwoko bw’umuntu burashobora kuboneka (desayuno), ariko mu Icyongereza ni cyagombwa kugena ‘I’ (‘I have breakfast’). Ubundi bindi bihambaye bikomeye: mu Icyongereza, kugena ibintu byoroshye, ubishusha ubwoko bw’umuntu bw’iminsi (he gets up), n’amagambo yo kugena ubwoko bw’umuntu bw’iminsi (‘always’, ‘usually’) ashushwa inyuma y’igisubizo, atari ku mwishywa nk’mu gaciri (‘siempre me levanto’ vs. ‘I always get up’).
rule: Kugena iby’uburo mu Icyongereza, ubishusha ubwoko bw’umuntu bw’iminsi (present simple). Ubwoko bw’umuntu bw’iminsi ni: Umuntu + igisubizo (na -s kuri he/she/it) + icyo kuri. Amagambo yo kugena ubwoko bw’umuntu bw’iminsi (always, usually, often, sometimes, never) ashushwa inyuma y’igisubizo kirekire, ariko inyuma y’igisubizo ‘to be’. Amagambo yo kugena ubwoko bw’umuntu bw’iminsi nk’‘in the morning’, ‘at night’ ashushwa ku mwishywa cyangwa ku mwishywa y’ijambo. Remera ko mu Icyongereza ntushobora kugena umuntu.

concept_examples.text: I wake up at six every morning.
concept_examples.phonetic: /aɪ weɪk ʌp æt sɪks ˈɛvri ˈmɔrnɪŋ/

concept_examples.text: She usually takes a shower in the evening.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ʃi ˈjuʒuəli teɪks ə ˈʃaʊər ɪn ðə ˈivnɪŋ/

concept_examples.text: We have breakfast together at home.
They always go to bed at eleven.
concept_examples.translation: Baremye barinda ku mbara z’amashuku yose.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ðeɪ ˈɔlweɪz goʊ tu bɛd æt ɪˈlɛvən/

common_error.explanation: Ibikorwa bikomeye ni guhunga -s mu bwoko bw’umuntu bw’umwe. Mu gaciri, ubwoko bw’umuntu bw’umwe burahinduka (‘se despierta’), ariko mu Icyongereza ubishusha -s cyangwa -es. Ubundi bikorwa ni kugena umuntu (‘Wakes up’), ariko mu Icyongereza ni cyagombwa. Kugira ngo ubihe, remera: na he/she/it, ubishusha -s ku igisubizo.

examples.note: Bishusha ‘get up’ kugira ngo ubure mu ibanga, atari ‘wake up’ kugira ngo ubure.
Mu Icyongereza, ubishusha igisubizo ‘his’, atari igisubizo ‘se’.
‘Have’ bishushwa kugira ngo ubure mu byo kurya n’ibyokwigwa, atari ‘drink’.

examples.original: They go to work by car.
examples.note: Bishusha ‘by’ + ububiko bw’ubucuruzi bw’umuntu (by car, by bus).
Igisubizo ‘after’ kirashobora kugenda ku mwishywa, nk’mu gaciri.
Na he/she/it, igisubizo ‘watch’ kirahinduka ‘watches’.

levels.label: Adverbs of Frequency
levels.translation: Amagambo yo kugena ubwoko bw’umuntu bw’iminsi

examples.original: I always eat lunch at noon.
examples.translation: Nkurya nyama za mbere ku mbara z’amashuku.
examples.note: Igisubizo ‘always’ kirashobora kugenda inyuma y’igisubizo ‘eat’, atari ku mwishywa.

examples.original: He usually reads the news in the morning.
examples.phonetic: /hi ˈjuʒuəli ridz ðə nuz ɪn ðə ˈmɔrnɪŋ/
examples.translation: Yaremye yongera akanywa amakuru mu gitondo.
examples.note: Igisubizo ‘usually’ kirashobora kugenda inyuma y’umuntu n’igisubizo.
‘Never’ ni igisubizo kirekire, ntibishushwa ‘don’t’ mu ijambo rimwe.

title: Talking about health and symptoms / Kuganira neza iby’ubuzima n’ibibazo
bridge: Mu gaciro, dushtura verb ‘gutanga’ kugirango tusuzume ibibazo nk’uko tugomba tugira ubwoba: ‘ndagiye n’ubwoba bw’umutwe’, ‘ndagiye n’ubwoba bw’amabara’. Mu Icyongereza, icyapfuye ni ukuri: tugomba tushtura ‘have’ (‘I have a headache’) kuri ibibazo n’ ‘feel’ kuri ibyo dusanga (‘I feel sick’). Ibibazo byinshi ni ukubwira ‘I have cold’ aho kubwira ‘I have a cold’, kubera mu Icyongereza ibibazo nk’ubwoba bw’amabara cyangwa ubwoba bw’umutwe birashobora kugira akamaro ka ‘a’. Nanone, remera ko ‘ache’ bishobora kugaragaza ibintu byinshi: ‘headache’, ‘toothache’, ariko ‘pain’ ni ibyago by’ubushishozi.
rule:
Kugirango wiganire neza iby’ubuzima n’ibibazo mu Icyongereza mu matora w’A2, ushture ibyo:

1. **Have + ibibazo:** Ushture ‘have’ (nta ‘gutanga’ mu buryo bw’inyoma) kuri ibibazo by’ubushishozi: ‘I have a cold’ (ndagiye n’ubwoba bw’amabara), ‘I have a headache’ (ndagiye n’ubwoba bw’umutwe), ‘I have a toothache’ (ndagiye n’ubwoba bw’amenyo). Remera ko ugomba gushtura akamaro ka ‘a’ mbere y’iby’ubushishozi.

2. **Feel + igitumo:** Kugirango usuzume ibyo usanga, ushture ‘feel’ + igitumo: ‘I feel tired’ (ndasanzwe n’ubushishozi), ‘I feel sick’ (ndasanzwe n’ubwoba), ‘I feel dizzy’ (ndasanzwe n’ubwoba bw’umutwe).

3. **Ubushishozi bw’ubushishozi:** Iyo ubushishozi ntibushoboye gusuzumwa, ushobora kubwira ‘I have pain in my back’ (ndagiye n’ubwoba bw’umutwe) cyangwa ‘my back hurts’ (umutwe wanjye ubara).

4. **Verbo ‘hurt’:** ‘Hurt’ bishobora kugaragaza ibyo ubara: ‘My head hurts’ (Umuntwe wanjye ubara), ‘My stomach hurts’ (Umubiri wanjye ubara).

5. **Kubaza iby’ubuzima:** Kugirango ubaze umwe iby’ubuzima: ‘What’s wrong?’ (Ni iki cyabaye?), ‘Are you okay?’ (Witeze neza?), ‘How do you feel?’ (Uteze gute?).

6. **Ibikorwa:** Kugirango ubere ibikorwa, ushture ‘should’ cyangwa ‘shouldn’t’: ‘You should see a doctor’ (Wigomeke kugera ku mubiri), ‘You shouldn’t eat that’ (Ntugomba kurya ibyo).

**Ibikorwa n’ibintu by’ubushishozi:**
- ‘Cold’ (ubwoba bw’amabara) ni iby’ubushishozi n’ibikorwa: ‘a cold’.
- ‘Flu’ (ubwoba bw’amabara) birashobora kugaragaza iby’ubushishozi: ‘I have the flu’ cyangwa ‘I have flu’, ariko ‘the flu’ ni iby’ubushishozi.
- ‘Fever’ (ubwoba bw’amabara) bishobora kugaragaza iby’ubushishozi: ‘I have a fever’.
- ‘Sore throat’ (ubwoba bw’umutwe) ntibishobora kugaragaza iby’ubushishozi: ‘I have a sore throat’? Ewe, bishobora kugaragaza iby’ubushishozi: ‘I have a sore throat’.
- Ibibazo byinshi ntibishobora kugaragaza iby’ubushishozi: ‘I have a cough’ (cyangwa ‘to cough’), ‘I have a runny nose’ (cyangwa ‘I have a runny nose’? aha bishobora kugaragaza iby’ubushishozi).

**Note:** Mu Icyongereza, nta ‘make’ kugaragaza ibibazo nk’mu gaciro (‘me duele’ = ‘it hurts’ cyangwa ‘I have pain’).

concept_examples.text: I have a headache.
I feel sick.
My stomach hurts.
You should see a doctor.

common_error.explanation: Mu gaciro, tusubira ‘ndagiye n’ubwoba bw’amabara’ cyangwa ‘ndagiye n’ubwoba bw’umutwe’ nta kamaro mu buryo bw’inyoma, ariko mu Icyongereza ‘cold’ (ubwoba bw’amabara) ni iby’ubushishozi n’ibikorwa n’akamaro ka ‘a’. ‘Have got’ ni iby’ubushishozi n’ibikorwa. Kugirango ubwire ‘ndagiye n’ubwoba bw’amabara’ (ubwoba bw’amabara), ushobora kubwira ‘I am cold’ cyangwa ‘I feel cold’, nta ‘I have cold’.

examples.note: Remura ko ‘a cough’ bishobora kugaragaza iby’ubushishozi. Mu gaciro, tusubira ‘ndagiye n’ubwoba bw’amabara’ nta kamaro mu buryo bw’inyoma.
Ubwoba bw’amabara bishobora kugaragaza iby’ubushishozi, ahandi ‘ndagiye n’ubwoba bw’amabara’ mu gaciro.
‘Sore throat’ ni iby’ubushishozi. Nta ‘pain in the throat’ mu buryo bw’inyoma.
Ushture ‘feel’ + igitumo kugirango usuzume ibyo usanga. Nta ‘I am having dizzy’.
‘Tired’ ni igitumo, nta verbo. Mu gaciro, tusubira ‘ndasanzwe n’ubushishozi’, mu Icyongereza ‘I feel tired’ cyangwa ‘I am tired’.
Ni ubushishozi bw’ubushishozi buhagaze kugirango ubaze ‘How are you?’ cyangwa ‘How do you feel?’.

levels.label: Giving and asking about health advice

examples.note: Ni ubushishozi bw’ubushishozi buhagaze kugirango ubaze umwe iby’ubuzima. Ni iby’ubushishozi.
Ushture ‘should’ + verbo mu buryo bw’inyoma kugirango ubere ibikorwa. Nta ‘should to rest’.
Verbo ni ‘take’ kuri mubiri, nta ‘drink’ cyangwa ‘eat’.
‘Shouldn’t’ ni iby’ubushishozi by’ubushishozi by’ubushishozi. Bishobora kugaragaza ibyo ntugomba kugura.

title: Making requests and offers / Gutegura n’ Kugisha ubufasha
bridge: Mu gaciri, dushtura imperatifi cyangwa ‘¿Puedes...?’ kugura ibintu, ariko mu gishinga ni byabanze kubyira ‘Can’ na ‘Could’ bishimwa neza. Kugisha ubufasha, abanyarwanda bavuga ‘¿Quieres que...?’, ariko mu gishinga bashimira ‘Can I...?’ cyangwa ‘Do you want me to...?’. Kanga ubwoba: mu gishinga, ‘Could you...?’ ni byinshi kurushaho kuri ‘Can you...?’, kandi ntushyireho imperatifi gusa kugura, kuba bishimwa neza gusa.
rule:
Kugura mu gishinga kuri ubwami A2, dushtura:
- 'Can you + verbo...?' (ntibishimwa neza, byabanze)
- 'Could you + verbo...?' (byinshi kurushaho n’ byishimwa neza)
- 'Would you mind + gerundio?' (byinshi kurushaho, ariko birinda).
Kugisha ubufasha:
- 'Can I + verbo...?' (¿Puedo...?)
- 'Do you want me to + verbo...?' (¿Quieres que...?)
- 'Would you like me to + verbo...?' (byinshi kurushaho).
Shima ko mu gishinga, umwugo uri hanyuma ya ‘Can’ cyangwa ‘Could’ ugomba kuba mu ndango yacyo ntibishimwa n’ ‘to’. Kugisha ubufasha, shiraho ‘me to’ hanyuma ya ‘want’ cyangwa ‘like’. Ntushyireho ‘Do you want that...’ nk’umu gaciri.

concept_examples.text: Can you help me with this?
Could you open the window, please?
Can I give you a hand?
Do you want me to get you a coffee?
concept_examples.phonetic: /duː juː wɒnt miː tə ɡet juː ə ˈkɒfi/

common_error.wrong: Do you want that I help you?
common_error.correct: Do you want me to help you?
common_error.explanation: Mu gaciri, twavuga ‘¿Quieres que te ayude?’, n’abanyeshuri bashaka kugira ubwoko bw’ibyo bavuga n’ ‘that I’. Mu gishinga, ubwoko bw’ibyo birushaho ni ‘want + umuntu + to + umwugo’, ntibishimwa ‘that + umuntu + umwugo’. Ubundi bwoko ni ‘Can I help you?’ ubishimwa neza n’uburyo bwo kugura.

examples.original: Can you pass me the salt?
examples.note: Ubushishozwe mu bihe by’uburozwe. ‘Pass me’ bishimwa ‘ndfashye’, ariko n’ ‘can’ bishimwa neza.
‘Can’ bishimwa kugura ibintu ntibishimwa neza kuri abahanganwe cyangwa abashishanyije.

examples.original: Can you speak more slowly, please?
examples.note: Ongeraho ‘please’ hanyuma kugira ngo ubishimwe neza.
Shyira ‘could’ kugira ngo ubishimwe neza cyangwa ubwo ntukubona neza umuntu.

examples.original: Could you bring us the menu, please?
examples.phonetic: /kʊd juː brɪŋ ʌs ðə ˈmenjuː pliːz/
examples.translation: Wishobora kuduha igitabo cy’ibyo dusanga, n’ubwenge?
examples.note: Mu nzu y’ibya kurya, ‘could’ ni byishimwa neza kurushaho kuri ‘can’.

examples.original: Could you help me carry these bags?
examples.phonetic: /kʊd juː help miː ˈkæri ðiːz bæɡz/
examples.note: Kugisha ubufasha byinshi, shiraho ‘could’ kugira ngo ubishimwe neza.

examples.original: Can I get you something to drink?
examples.phonetic: /kæn aɪ ɡet juː ˈsʌmθɪŋ tə drɪŋk/
examples.note: Ubushishozwe kugisha ubufasha, bishimwa ‘Wishikuye kugushimira ikinyobwa?’.

examples.original: Do you want me to help you with that?
examples.phonetic: /duː juː wɒnt miː tə help juː wɪð ðæt/
examples.note: Ubwoko bw’ibyo ‘want + me + to’ kugisha ubufasha bisanzwe.

examples.original: Would you like me to open the window?
examples.phonetic: /wʊd juː laɪk miː tə ˈəʊpən ðə ˈwɪndəʊ/
examples.note: Byinshi kurushaho kuri ‘do you want me to’. Birinda mu bihe by’ubushakashatsi cyangwa n’abantu ntukubona.

title: Expressing Ability and Possibility / Kugena ubushakashatsi na kugena ubwoko
bridge: Kugena ubushakashatsi, mu gacika, harimo 'poder' kuri ubushakashatsi na 'saber' kuri kumenya gutora icimosa. Mu Icyongereza, ibyo bibiri bikombanywa mu nshingano 'can' (mu cyo nyine) na 'could' (mu cyashize), ariko kuba cyubahwa: 'could' ntibiyongereka kugena ibyakozwe mu cyashize (bimenye, 'Could you swim?') na 'be able to' biyongereka mu gihe 'can' ntibikaba. Nanone, kugena ubwoko, 'can' na 'could' bigenamo ubwoko bwitegekanijwe, 'may' na 'might' bigenamo ubwoko buri mu buryo, ibintu ntibikaba mu gacika mu buryo bwo kugamburukira.
rule: Kugena ubushakashatsi mu cyo nyine, onga 'can' + inshingano ya mbere (bimenye, 'I can swim'). Mu cyashize, kugena ubushakashatsi bwitegekanijwe, onga 'could' + inshingano ya mbere (bimenye, 'I could swim when I was young'). Kugena ibikorwa byakozwe mu cyashize (ibyakozwe), onga 'was/were able to' (nti 'could'). Kugena ubwoko, 'can' bigena ubwoko bwitegekanijwe (bimenye, 'It can rain'), 'could' bigena ubwoko bwashize cyangwa bwitegekanijwe (bimenye, 'It could rain later'), 'may' na 'might' bigenamo ubwoko buri mu buryo (bimenye 'She may come'). Ubuvomo bw'inshingano 'can' ni 'cannot' cyangwa 'can't', bw'inshingano 'could' ni 'couldn't'. Ntimwongere 'to' nyuma y'inshingano 'can' cyangwa 'could'.

concept_examples.text: I can speak English and Spanish.
Could you help me, please?
She might be at home now.
concept_examples.translation: Yebwe yoba ari mu rugo ubu.

concept_examples.text: We were able to find the hotel after asking.
concept_examples.phonetic: /wiː wɜːr ˈeɪbəl tə faɪnd ðə hoʊˈtɛl ˈæftər ˈæskɪŋ/

common_error.wrong: I can to play the guitar.
common_error.explanation: Mu gacika, tugamba 'puedo tocar', no kuri 'a' bimwe, kandi harimo ubwenge bwo kugabanya 'to' nyuma y'inshingano 'can'. Ariko mu Icyongereza, 'can' bihaguruka direct mu nshingano ya mbere, bitagira 'to'. Remera: can + inshingano ya mbere, ntibyoba can + to + inshingano.

examples.note: Onga 'can' kugena ko uzi gutora icimosa. Reba ko mu gacika bigaragara 'saber' cyangwa 'poder', ahubwo mu Icyongereza 'can' gusa.
Mu ibazu, hindura ubwoko: 'Can' + umuntu + inshingano.
Ubuvomo ni 'can't' (ubwoko bw'inshingano 'cannot').

levels.label: Ability and Possibility in the Past

examples.original: When I was a child, I could run fast.
examples.phonetic: /wɛn aɪ wəz ə tʃaɪld, aɪ kʊd rʌn fæst/
examples.translation: Igihe nari umwana, narashobora gutwara neza.
examples.note: Onga 'could' kugena ubushakashatsi bwitegekanijwe mu cyashize.

examples.original: I was able to finish the exam yesterday.
examples.phonetic: /aɪ wəz ˈeɪbəl tə ˈfɪnɪʃ ði ɪɡˈzæm ˈjɛstərdeɪ/
examples.note: Kugena ibikorwa byakozwe mu cyashize, ntimwongere 'could', ahubwo 'was/were able to'.
Mu cyashize, 'could' nanone bigenamo ubwoko.
Onga 'may' kuba ububasha bwitegekanijwe.
Onga 'might' kugena ubwoko buri mu buryo, hasi no kuva mu mbere.
Mu Icyongereza idacukije, 'can' biyongereka kuba ububasha.

title: Talking about weather / Kuganira iby’ijoro
bridge: Mu gaciri, dusubiza ‘hace calor’ cyangwa ‘está lloviendo’, tukoresha amatsiko ‘hacer’ cyangwa ‘estar’. Mu Icyongereza, ijoro riganirwa na pronome ‘it’ nk’umusubirizi: ‘It is hot’, ‘It is raining’. Ubu burenganzira ni ukwunguka kubera ko mu Icyongereza ntidushakiye umusubirizi w’yonyine, kandi mu gaciri harakoreshwa. Ubundi bungororoka ni ko ‘weather’ mu Icyongereza ntikorwa, bityo ntidusubiza ‘a weather’ cyangwa ‘weathers’.
rule:
Kuganira iby’ijoro mu Icyongereza A2, koresha ibyo mbuga:
1. 'It is' + adjectif: It is sunny, It is cloudy, It is windy, It is cold, It is warm.
2. 'It is' + verbe mu gerundio kugir’iby’igikorwa: It is raining, It is snowing, It is hailing.
3. 'There is' + ishusho: There is a storm, There is fog, There is a rainbow.
4. 'There are' + amashusho yo hamwe: There are clouds, There are showers.

Ibikorwa n’ubushishozi: ‘It is hot’ na ‘It is cold’ ni bikoreshwa, ariko no koresha ‘It's warm’ na ‘It's cool’. Kugera urushohoza, koresha ‘What's the weather like?’ cyangwa ‘How's the weather?’ (ntukoreshe ‘How is the weather?’). Remera ko ‘weather’ ntikorwa: ntukavuga ‘a weather’.

concept_examples.text: It is sunny today.
It is raining outside.
It is very cold in winter.
There are some clouds in the sky.
concept_examples.translation: Hari amagufa ahantu hasi mu kirere.
concept_examples.phonetic: /ðər ər sʌm klaʊdz ɪn ðə skaɪ/

common_error.explanation: Mu gaciri, dusubiza ‘el tiempo está caliente’ cyangwa ‘hace calor’, n’abanyeshuri bakunda kugira ubugereranyije. Ariko mu Icyongereza, kuganira iby’ijoro, tukoresha ‘it’ nk’umusubirizi, ntukoresha ‘the weather’. Kuvuga ‘the weather is hot’ bitangira neza; ibyiza ni ‘It is hot’. Ubundi, remera ko ‘hot’ bishimira ubushyuhe, ntijoro mu binyejana.

examples.note: ‘Sunny’ bikoreshwa kuganira umunsi uri na solel. Mu gaciri dusubiza ‘hari urushushi’.
‘Cloudy’ bikoreshwa igihe hari amagufa menshi. Mu gaciri dusubiza ‘iryenyabwenge ryararohoye’.
‘Windy’ bishimira ikindi gishyize. Ntukibigirire na ‘wind’ (ishusho).
Kugir’ubushyuhe bw’ubushyuhe. ‘Cold’ no koresha kuganira ibintu cyangwa abantu.
Tukoresha ‘be + -ing’ kugir’iby’igikorwa gishyashye. Mu gaciri, dusubiza ‘iryenyabwenge ryararohoye’.
Gusa mu bihugu by’ubushyuhe. ‘Snow’ ni ishusho, ‘snowing’ ni umusubirizi.
‘Hail’ ni ishusho y’amabere. Ntikoreshwa cyane, ariko birahinda.
Ubu buganiro bishimira ko amagufa yarakaye kandi urushushi rwakuye.
Urushohoza rw’ibya mbere. Koresha ‘like’ mu maganiro.

examples.original: It will be rainy on Friday.
examples.translation: Iryenyabwenge rizaba ryararohora ku wa gatatu.
examples.note: Koresha ‘will’ kugir’ibya mbere. ‘Rainy’ ni adjectif, ‘raining’ ni umusubirizi.

examples.original: It is going to snow tonight.
examples.note: ‘Going to’ bikoreshwa kugir’amategeko y’ibya mbere (amagufa, n.k.).

examples.original: There will be a storm tomorrow.
examples.note: Koresha ‘there will be’ kugir’ibintu byiza kubaho mu mbere.
